items.title: Jewish hospital patient 'paralysed with fear' after threatening video, royal commission hears
items.description: A Jewish NSW Health worker and patient who says she experienced antisemitism in the workplace tells the royal commission she considered cancelling her knee surgery after becoming "paralysed" with fear in the wake of two nurses making threats against Israeli patients.

items.title: This island was once ruled by Australia. Now, it could become the world's newest country
items.description: A tropical archipelago just 1,500 kilometres from Australia is readying to become the world's newest country. But as Bougainville nears independence, memories of a bloody past are coming back to the surface.

items.title: Gas bills 'no longer hostage' to international market under new laws to drop price
items.description: A new east coast gas reserve will "drive down" prices, according to the federal government and ensure Australia is no longer "hostage" to international markets.

items.title: British PM Keir Starmer braces for ballot box backlash
items.description: They might be local elections, but the results of thousands of votes being held on Thursday around Britain are likely to have major ramifications for the national government.

items.title: Live: Israel strikes Beirut for first time since Hezbollah ceasefire, Iran weighs up a peace deal
items.description: The strikes come as Iran weighs up a peace deal put forward by the US, with Donald Trump saying the war could "be at an end". Follow live.

items.title: 'Like paradise': Women and children with IS-links excited to return to Australia
items.description: Australian authorities are preparing for the arrival of 13 women and children linked to Islamic State fighters, some of whom face possible arrest. Some are on a flight from Doha to Melbourne, while another flight is expected to land in Sydney. The federal government has always maintained that while it would not help the ISIS-linked families get home, it doesn't have the power to stop them.  ABC correspondent Bridget Rollason is on a flight and has spoken to some of the families.

items.title: Why this firebrand leader's defeat is hailed as a win for democracy in India
items.description: Mamata Banerjee was once considered a threat to India's Narendra Modi. But now, her historic defeat due to "misrule" has the Indian Opposition in tatters.

items.title: Major data breach sees student details compromised
items.description: Education institutions around the country are scrambling to respond to a global data breach that has affected Australian universities, TAFE and state schools in Queensland.

items.title: Former Test cricketer was drinking wine before breath test, lawyer says
items.description: Former Australian Test cricketer David Warner will accept responsibility for a "reckless", "foolish" and "wrong" decision that resulted in a mid-range drink driving charge, his lawyer says.

items.title: Kyle and Jackie O war costs ARN Media $26 million
items.description: ARN Media reveals "brand safety" concerns over the Kyle and Jackie O Show have cost the company tens of millions in advertising revenue.

items.title: One answer to Australia's housing affordability crisis is hidden in plain sight
items.description: What if the sudden improvement in Iain's life, and the extra $600 a month in his pocket, can be traced back to a single policy decision made by a federal minister in the 1980s?

items.title: Live: ASX gains in global rally, Tabcorp crashes on money laundering probe
items.description: The ASX's earlier gains have been being trimmed as Tabcorp's shares are crunched on news of a fresh money laundering investigation. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: As LIV struggles, Adelaide secures men’s Australian Open golf tournament
items.description: After weeks of political pressure over the future of LIV Golf, the South Australian government has secured the men's Australian Open, set to be held at the redeveloped North Adelaide Golf Course from 2028 in a spilt with another state.

items.title: New gas field in waters near Twelve Apostles given green light
items.description: The gas field off the south-west coast of Victoria could provide up to 4 per cent of the east coast's energy supplies.

items.title: Can you identify Aussie movies from a single frame?
items.description: Think you know your Moulin Rouge from your Muriel's Wedding? Take our Australian movie quiz to prove you're the king of The Castle.

items.title: How the Tokyo Metro became the terrifying setting for film Exit 8
items.description: The creator of the minimalist horror film hopes it inspires viewers to stop doomscrolling and take a look at the world around them.

items.title: Bushfires now burn at a 'whole different level'. It means rethinking volunteers
items.description: Bushfires are occurring at a new level of ferocity across Australia. It could leave our volunteers overpowered.

items.title: Leaders call for child protection reviews ahead of Kumanjayi Little Baby vigils
items.description: As memorials for Kumanjayi Little Baby are held across the country, leaders call for a review of the child protection system to ensure the safety of young people is prioritised.

items.title: Is Richard Dawkins right about AI?
items.description: Is AI conscious? Richard Dawkins is asking the wrong question.

items.title: Albanese's budget won't be derailed by Trump's pronouncements
items.description: It's clear that whatever this unpredictable US president says, the Albanese government isn't expecting a return to normal oil flows any time soon.

items.title: Carnarvon shire council will receive commissioner after mass resignations
items.description: WA's local government minister will appoint a commissioner to Carnarvon Shire following mass council resignations.

items.title: Passengers say 'ghost bookings' now common on crucial V/Line service
items.description: Public transport passengers in Victoria's north-west say a rise in "ghost bookings" has led to half-empty bus services during the state's free transport period.

items.title: Victorians wake to snow month out from ski season
items.description: Snow has fallen on Victoria's higher peaks overnight, as below-zero temperatures blast the state.

items.title: Federation Square to host World Cup events after premier's intervention
items.description: Screenings of the FIFA World Cup will go ahead at Federation Square later this year after the Victorian premier overturned an unpopular decision to not host fans at the precinct.

items.title: A device saved Rory's life. Now Canberrans can access one in every suburb
items.description: Rory was spending his night like any other 16-year-old, playing sports with friends, when the unthinkable happened. He went into cardiac arrest.
